Northern Sakhalin stays Ainu land because the status was left open until the Treaty of Saint Petersburg (1875), although Cliopatria's Russian Empire shape holds 165 of its 174 cells from about 1857. ledger.note: 13th century: the Ainu culture. 'The Ainu culture developed from the 13th century (late Kamakura period)'; the page links it to the Satsumon culture and gives no territory. The land is the 1868 distribution of the Ainu (researcher's reading, confidence 1); the Emishi's descendants were pushed north from the 9th century, a descent, not a handover of land. Satsumon culture page (700-1200): 'a partially agricultural, archeological culture of northern Honshu and southern Hokkaido', 'regarded to be ancestral to the later Ainu culture'; it names no Sakhalin or Kurils, so the 1200 extent beyond southern Hokkaido stays the 1868 distribution. History of Hokkaido: the Ainu 'extended their domain to a large part of Sakhalin and the entire Kuril Islands' (undated, [citation needed]).

notes:
Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from five pages (Ainu people, Koshamain, Shakushain's revolt, Menashi-Kunashir rebellion, History of Hokkaido); repaired the same day after the reviewer's fail verdict, with seven more pages (Treaty of Shimoda, Treaty of Saint Petersburg, Kuril Islands, Hakodate bugyo, Satsumon culture, Ezo, Matsumae Domain). The Ainu are a people with village chiefdoms, not a state; typed state so that the Wajin and Russian expansion into Ezo, Sakhalin and the Kurils has a counterpart. Start 1200 is the page's 13th century; the extent is the 1868 distribution, not a boundary (Satsumon culture page: northern Honshu and southern Hokkaido only). No capital, no rulers.
Repair 2026-10-19: (1) eastern Ezo returns in 1822 (gain from tokugawa-shogunate, confidence 1, mirror of matsumae-domain /ledger/7 and tokugawa-shogunate /ledger/8) and the 1807 keyframe is split at 1822. (2) The Kurils are divided at the Shimoda line in February 1855: 13 cells to tokugawa-shogunate, 8 cells to russian-empire; the northernmost 7 cells go to the Russian shape from 1748 (confidence 1); 3 central cells remain to 1875. (3) The 1869 loss of Hokkaido is dropped: Hokkaido left the Ainu shape in 1855 (History of Hokkaido: shogunate control of most of Ezochi 1855-1858; annexed and renamed by Japan in 1869). (4) vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart matsumae-domain are added for 1672, 1799, 1822 and 1855 (mirrors on the vassal side; the tint is drawn from matsumae-domain). (5) 1264 is booked to mongol-empire with a 1293/1294 handoff to yuan-dynasty, as the page says 'the Mongols'.
Open points. The 1799-1806 and 1822 dates: the Ainu page ends direct rule in 1806 and the Ezo, Matsumae Domain and Hakodate bugyo pages say nothing of 1807-1821 or the return, so Cliopatria's Tokugawa shape of 1799-1821 is followed; 1807 'western Ezo' is not drawn. Disagreements: Koshamain's counteroffensive is 1458 on the page, the ashikaga-shogunate dossier dates the Wajin regain to 1459; Cliopatria's Tokugawa shape adds Hokkaido in 1856, this dossier and matsumae-domain say 1855; Cliopatria's Russian Empire shape holds 165 of the 174 northern Sakhalin cells from about 1857, while both treaty pages leave Sakhalin's status open to 1875, so northern Sakhalin stays Ainu land here and the renderer should treat it as contested with russian-empire (tokugawa-shogunate has a contest from 1855). The Sakhalin split at 50 N is a reading of 'southern Sakhalin' (Karafuto's later border). Routed to other dossiers (not edited here): tokugawa-shogunate needs counterpart 'ainu' instead of 'nobody' for Ezo (1799, 1822, 1855, 1856), a southern Sakhalin gain in 1807 and a Kuril counterpart for 1855; empire-of-japan gains the northern Kurils in 1877 from russian-empire while the Ainu line is 1875 and has no 1869 Hokkaido counterpart to this dossier; russian-empire has no dossier yet to carry the 1748 and 1855 Kuril gains; mongol-empire and yuan-dynasty have no dossier yet to carry the Sakhalin contest. Not on the pages: Kamchatka, a Sakhalin Ainu relocation in 1875. Area comparison not applicable (no infobox area).
